regime.paragraph: Markets moved without a single dominant theme: US Treasury yields 2Y -3bp to 4.85% and 10Y +1bp to 5.14%. The US curve saw a twist steepener in 2s10s (+4bp to 29bp). The dollar rose 0.2%, gold rose 0.1%, the S&P 500 fell 0.4% and Brent rose 0.3%. US high-yield spreads tightened 10bp. The standout move was Germany 30Y Bund (+5bp, 1.9x its 20-day volatility).

regions.name: United States
regions.text: Treasuries rallied with the front end leading, 2Y -3bp to 4.85% and 10Y +1bp to 5.14%: a twist steepener (2s10s +4bp). Fed pricing was steady at +99bp over 12 months. The dollar rose 0.2% and the S&P 500 fell 0.4%.

regions.name: United Kingdom
regions.text: Gilts sold off with the long end leading, 2Y -1bp to 4.97% and 10Y +3bp to 5.34%: a twist steepener (2s10s +4bp). Gilts underperformed Treasuries by 3bp at 10Y. Markets added 6bp of BoE tightening over 12 months (now +99bp). Sterling fell 0.1% and the FTSE 100 rose 0.4%.

regions.name: Europe
regions.text: Bunds sold off with the long end leading, 2Y -1bp to 3.11% and 10Y +5bp to 3.38%: a twist steepener (2s10s +6bp). BTP-Bund was steady 0bp to 105bp. Markets added 3bp of ECB tightening over 12 months on the bill-curve proxy (now +71bp). The euro fell 0.3% and the Euro Stoxx 50 fell 0.2%.

regions.name: Japan
regions.text: JGB 10Y yields rose 7bp to 2.857%, with 30Y +8bp. The yen strengthened as USD/JPY moved -0.1% to 159.69. Markets added 4bp of BoJ tightening over 12 months on the bill-curve proxy (now +97bp). The Nikkei fell 2.1%.

regions.name: China
regions.text: CGB 10Y yields rose 1bp to 1.60%. The renminbi weakened with USD/CNY +0.02% at 6.6718. The CSI 300 fell 0.7% and copper fell 2.0%.

relationships.statement: EUR/USD fell even as the Treasury–Bund spread narrowed.
relationships.lesson: FX tends to follow relative rates: a wider US–German yield gap raises the carry on USD versus EUR. Front-end (2Y) differentials usually matter more than 10Y.

relationships.statement: The Treasury curve twisted steeper: easier near-term policy but more long-run risk premium.
relationships.lesson: Front end rallied while the long end sold off: easier policy expected but more long-run risk.

relationships.statement: Higher UK 30Y yields, outpacing Treasuries, suggested rising UK term premium and fiscal supply concerns.
relationships.lesson: When long gilts underperform without a matching front-end move, the market is demanding more compensation for duration: issuance, fiscal credibility and pension demand matter most.

interview.question: Why did the German 2Y outperform the 10Y?
interview.answer: The German 2Y moved -1bp and the 10Y +5bp, so 2s10s moved +6bp to 26bp: a twist steepener. Front end rallied while the long end sold off: easier policy expected but more long-run risk. Market pricing for the ECB over 12 months moved +3bp, which is what drives the front end. Key framework: the 2Y is anchored by expected policy over two years; the 10Y adds term premium and long-run growth and inflation expectations.

interview.question: Why did the UK 2Y outperform the 10Y?
interview.answer: The UK 2Y moved -1bp and the 10Y +3bp, so 2s10s moved +4bp to 37bp: a twist steepener. Front end rallied while the long end sold off: easier policy expected but more long-run risk. Market pricing for the BoE over 12 months moved +6bp, which is what drives the front end. Key framework: the 2Y is anchored by expected policy over two years; the 10Y adds term premium and long-run growth and inflation expectations.

interview.question: What is the market pricing for the Bank of England, and what changed today?
interview.answer: Policy rate 4.00%. Markets price a 76% chance of a 25bp hike at the next meeting and 4.0 hikes (99bp) over 12 months; terminal 5.01%. The 12-month pricing moved +6bp on the day. Method: Bank of England SONIA OIS curve. Remember that one 25bp move is 25bp of pricing, so +99bp is 4.0 moves.

interview.question: Why did Treasuries outperform Bunds?
interview.answer: 10Y Treasuries moved +1bp versus +5bp for Bunds, so the spread moved -4bp to 176bp (98th percentile of the past year). Cross-market spreads remove the global rates move and isolate local drivers: domestic data surprises, relative central-bank repricing, and supply or fiscal news. Check whether the front end (2Y spread) moved too: if it did, it is a policy story; if only the long end moved, it is term premium.

interview.question: What is the market pricing for the Bank of Japan, and what changed today?
interview.answer: Policy rate 1.04%. Markets price a 73% chance of a 25bp hike at the next meeting and 3.9 hikes (97bp) over 12 months; terminal 2.19%. The 12-month pricing moved +4bp on the day. Method: Government bill-curve proxy (indicative). Remember that one 25bp move is 25bp of pricing, so +97bp is 3.9 moves.

flashcards.front: Where is US 2s10s, and what did it do today?
How much Fed easing or tightening is priced over 12 months?
What was today's largest volatility-adjusted move?
What is a bear steepener, and what usually causes it?
flashcards.back: Yields rise with the long end rising more than the front. Usually term premium, fiscal supply or inflation risk, not a policy repricing.
